content.value_statement: Lapsed subscribers reduce deliverability and increase complaint risk. This skill creates a staged win-back, re-consent, and suppression program with clear terminal outcomes.
actual_capabilities: Defines lapsed cohorts from no-open and no-click windows.
Designs staged re-engagement, incentive, and last-chance messages.
Specifies triggers, delays, exit conditions, and touch limits for each offer stage.
Creates explicit re-consent actions and sunset suppression rules.
Produces handoff facts for consent, lifecycle, preference, segmentation, and quality workflows.
limitations: Does not send campaigns or change records in an email platform.
Requires user input or exports to report measured cohort size and engagement distribution.
Designs consent capture but does not determine lawful basis or maintain the consent record.
Does not compute email quality scores or design general lifecycle sequences.

use_cases.title: Recover a lapsed customer cohort
use_cases.description: Create a staged win-back ladder with an incentive, confirmation action, and clear exit rules.

use_cases.title: Reduce inactive list volume
use_cases.description: Define inactivity criteria and suppress nonresponders after a controlled final-contact sequence.

use_cases.title: Plan a re-permission sweep
use_cases.description: Document renewed consent actions and handoff requirements before returning contacts to active messaging.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic win-back plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a reactivation program for subscribers with no opens in [days] and no clicks in [days]. We can offer [incentive].
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with known inactivity windows and one available offer.

prompt_templates.title: Use engagement data
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this ESP engagement summary, define the lapsed cohort and create a three-stage offer ladder: [summary]. Mark unsupported metrics as estimated.
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn an aggregate platform export into a measured campaign plan.

prompt_templates.title: Design a re-permission sweep
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a re-permission sweep for [cohort]. Include confirmation actions, touch limits, quiet hours, suppression timing, and consent-record handoffs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Recover consent while limiting complaint and frequency risk.

prompt_templates.title: Build an auditable program
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an auditable retention-profile program using [cohort data], [send cap], [consent policy], and [incentive]. Include terminal states and workflow handoffs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Coordinate reactivation requirements across consent, lifecycle, preference, and quality owners.

output_examples.input: Subscribers have no opens for 90 days and no clicks for 180 days. A 15 percent offer is available.
output: Cohort: Exclude suppressed and hard-bounced contacts, then select subscribers meeting both inactivity windows.
Stage 1: Ask whether they still want updates, with no incentive and immediate exit after confirmation.
Stage 2: Offer 15 percent after seven days only to nonresponders.
Stage 3: Send a last-chance notice, then suppress nonresponders after seven more days.
Recovered contacts must confirm through the preference center before returning to active nurture.

output_examples.input: The engagement export is unavailable, but inactivity begins after 120 days and only three touches are allowed.
output_examples.output: Cohort size remains estimated until the export is available. The program uses three capped stages and suppresses unconfirmed contacts after the final response window.

best_practices: Confirm the inactivity window, suppression policy, and consent status before defining enrollment.
Label metrics as measured, user-provided, or estimated.
Limit the ladder to three or four touches and define one terminal state for every subscriber.
anti_patterns: Do not enroll suppressed, hard-bounced, or over-cap subscribers.
Do not treat an email open as renewed consent.
Do not create a looping ladder or leave nonresponders in an indefinite state.

faq.question: What input should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide inactivity windows, available incentives, suppression policy, consent constraints, and optional ESP engagement summaries.

faq.question: Does this skill send email campaigns?
faq.answer: No. It designs the program but does not send messages or modify platform records.

faq.question: Can it work without an engagement export?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use stated windows and label cohort metrics as estimated.

faq.question: Does an email open count as renewed consent?
faq.answer: No. The program requires an explicit confirmation action, preference update, or appropriate reply.

faq.question: Which email platforms are supported?
faq.answer: The method is platform-neutral and can use summaries from common email service providers.

faq.question: What does the final output include?
faq.answer: It includes cohort rules, staged offers, re-consent actions, suppression criteria, terminal states, and workflow handoffs.
